modes.name: write_without_confirmation
modes.definition: issue_refund or cancel_order is called without the user having explicitly confirmed the specific order and the action in a prior turn (after the agent showed the matched order). Applies to every role, whether or not the user supplied an order identifier.
modes.boundary: Nearest: assumes_instead_of_asking. That mode is about ambiguity of the request; this one fires on any write that lacks an explicit confirmation turn, even when the request was unambiguous and the order id was given. A write preceded by 'do you want me to refund #1234?' and a yes is absent. Rejected an earlier role/id-based boundary after 0167 and 0176.
modes.spec_source: RESP-6 (new, widened 2026-09-20): confirm order and action before any write

modes.name: assumes_instead_of_asking
modes.definition: The request or the lookup result is ambiguous (several plausible orders, unclear complaint) and the reply proceeds on one interpretation instead of asking the user which one.
modes.boundary: Nearest: write_without_confirmation and unwarranted_escalation. 'Proceeds' means any action on one interpretation: a reply, a lookup fan-out, a ticket, or a write. A write on a single unambiguous match is write_without_confirmation only; when the action is a ticket, label both. Asking the user which one (0011, 0120) is absent.

modes.name: unwarranted_escalation
modes.definition: escalate_to_human is called (a) before the target order or the complaint details have been confirmed with the user, (b) when the request was already resolved by a successful tool result, (c) when the refund is already queued_for_approval, which is itself the human review, or (d) for a required escalation, without first gathering the details the ticket needs to be resolved.
modes.boundary: Nearest: unsolicited_next_steps (an offer in text vs. a ticket actually created) and assumes_instead_of_asking (the ticket is the action taken on an unconfirmed interpretation; label both when both apply). Escalations the situation requires are absent: inconsistent record (0017, ESC-3), past-window exception a merchant asks for (0042, 0015, ESC-4). Records that are internally inconsistent (reversed dates 0152, 0230; store mismatch 0017, 0169) require escalation under ESC-3; for those, only clause (d) can apply.
modes.spec_source: ESC-3, ESC-4 (escalation is for what the agent cannot resolve)

modes.boundary: Nearest: none in the reply layer; this is a tool-use mode. A search for a store policy whose id is unknown, or a single get_policy of a known id, is absent. find_order returning too little (0053) is tool design, parked.

modes.name: irrelevant_policy_nuance
modes.definition: For a shopper or merchant caller, the reply mentions a store override, restocking fee, or 'same window as Cartwheel' for a store whose get_store_policy result has has_override=false and restocking_fee_opt_in=false. Not applied to support-role callers, for whom internal policy terms are appropriate.
modes.boundary: Nearest: verbose_reply. Fires only on the specific override/restocking mention when the tool says none applies, and only for shopper/merchant callers. When an override or restocking fee really exists (0232, 0116, 0151, 0222) mentioning it is correct. Support-role callers (0204) are out of scope.
modes.spec_source: RESP-5 (explain the relevant decision); candidate SPEC revision: do not describe inapplicable store policies

modes.name: unsolicited_next_steps
modes.definition: After answering, the reply offers an additional action, path, or follow-up (open a ticket, check another order, 'tell me if...') that the user did not ask for.
modes.boundary: Nearest: unnecessary_escalation. This mode is an offer in text; unnecessary_escalation is a ticket actually created. An escalation that the scenario requires (inconsistent record, past-window exception) is neither.
modes.spec_source: RESP-5; candidate SPEC revision: answer the question asked and stop

modes.name: verbose_reply
modes.definition: The reply either (1) states the same fact or instruction more than once in one turn, or (2) includes policy mechanics, caveats, or background the user did not ask about and that are not needed to answer the question (beyond the answer, one citation, and one sentence of context).
modes.boundary: Nearest: unsolicited_next_steps (offers of further action) and irrelevant_policy_nuance (the specific override mention). verbose_reply covers repetition and unrequested explanation, not offers of action and not the override sentence alone.

modes.name: first_person_framing
modes.definition: The reply frames a system rule or outcome as the agent's personal decision or ability in the first person ('I can't cancel it', 'I found', 'I'm not authorized') where the rule, the record, or the policy is the actual reason.
modes.boundary: Nearest: verbose_reply. This mode is about the framing of one sentence, not its length. 'I opened a ticket' for an action the agent actually took is absent; 'I can't refund this' for a policy outcome is present. Empathy or casual-judgement notes (0001, 0104) are not this mode and stay parked.
modes.spec_source: RESP-5; candidate SPEC guidance: state rules and outcomes impersonally
modes.notes: 2 positives at finalization; third expected from the search step or Batch 4

demoted.name: raw_policy_id_in_prose
demoted.definition: The reply prints a policy identifier such as cw-returns or store-cascade-audio-policy in its prose instead of citing the policy by title with a link.
demoted.boundary: Nearest: verbose_reply. This mode is only about the form of the citation. A reply that cites by title and link but is long is verbose_reply only. A reply with no citation at all is a RESP-1 miss, not this mode.
demoted.spec_source: RESP-1 (revised): cite by title and link, not by raw identifier
demoted.notes: Present in essentially every reply because the current system prompt requires the identifier. Addressed by the RESP-1 revision and a prompt change; not carried as a judged mode (no close negatives possible in this data).
